title: 第一卷 第3章 修史馆的老先生
slug: 大明死谏一百次老朱破防了
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

“陛下，臣怕得要死，”程壑川说，“臣跪在朝堂上的时候，腿在发抖。走进这个屋子的时候，臣闻到这里的气味，胃里翻江倒海。”

“臣怕死，怕得要命。”

“但臣更怕一件事。”

“什么事？”

“臣怕有一天，史书上写洪武年间，杀尽忠臣良将，其后朝中竟无人可用。”

“你很会说话，”朱元璋站起来，背着手在屋里踱步，“但光会说话没用。朕要的是能做事的人。”

“《元史》修得一塌糊涂，朕给你三个月，你去把它重修一遍。修好了，朕给你升官。修不好——”

朱元璋走到门口，回头看了他一眼。

“修不好，朕再跟你算今天这笔账。”

说完，朱元璋头也不回地走了。

脚步声越来越远，消失在走廊的尽头。

程壑川坐在冰冷的椅子上，整个人像被抽空了一样。

他没死。

他真的没死。

膝盖一软，这次是真的站不住了。

他扶着桌沿缓缓滑坐在地上，后背全是冷汗，整个人像是刚从水里捞出来的。

“程大人，”锦衣卫统领面无表情地说，“请吧。”

程壑川撑着站起来，腿还在抖。

走出刑讯室的时候，他最后回头看了一眼这个房间。

油灯还亮着，火苗在风里晃了晃。

锦衣卫的“暗中监视”，做得一点都不暗中。

程壑川走出诏狱的时候，身后就跟了个穿飞鱼服的校尉，明目张胆地缀在三十步开外，连装都不装一下。

那意思很明确：陛下在看，你最好老实点。

程壑川没管他。

他现在满脑子就一件事，三个月重修《元史》。

听起来像个闲差，但他知道这事一点都不闲。

元朝的历史本来就乱，朱元璋又是个较真的人，对现在这个版本极其不满。

原版《元史》他翻过，确实粗制滥造，前后矛盾的地方一大堆。

"Your Majesty, I am scared to death," Cheng Hechuan said. "When I was kneeling in the court hall, my legs were shaking. When I walked into this room, I smelled the smell here and my stomach turned upside down."

"I'm afraid of death. I'm scared to death."

"But Chen is more afraid of one thing."

"What's the matter?"

"I'm afraid that one day, it will be written in the history books that during the Hongwu period, all the loyal ministers and good generals were killed, and then there would be no one available in the court."

"You are good at talking," Zhu Yuanzhang stood up and paced around the room with his hands behind his back, "but it is useless just to talk. What I want is someone who can do things."

"The "History of the Yuan Dynasty" is a complete mess. I will give you three months to revise it again. If you fix it, I will give you a promotion. If you can't fix it well——"

Zhu Yuanzhang walked to the door and looked back at him.

"If you can't fix it, I'll settle the debt with you again today."

After saying that, Zhu Yuanzhang left without looking back.

The footsteps got farther and farther and disappeared at the end of the corridor.

Cheng Hechuan sat on the cold chair, as if his whole body had been emptied out.

He's not dead.

He's really not dead.

My knees went weak and I really couldn't stand this time.

He slowly slid to the ground while holding on to the edge of the table. His back was covered in cold sweat, and he looked like he had just been fished out of the water.

"Master Cheng," the commander of the Jin Yiwei said expressionlessly, "please."

Cheng Hechuan stood up, his legs still shaking.

As he walked out of the torture chamber, he took one last look back at the room.

The oil lamp was still on, the flame swaying in the wind.

Jin Yiwei's "secret surveillance" was not secretive at all.

When Cheng Hechuan walked out of the imperial prison, he was followed by a captain in a Feiyu uniform, blatantly standing thirty steps away without even pretending.

The meaning is clear: Your Majesty is watching, you'd better be honest.

Cheng Hechuan ignored him.

There is only one thing on his mind right now, which is to rewrite "History of the Yuan Dynasty" in three months.

It sounded like an idle job, but he knew it was anything but idle.

The history of the Yuan Dynasty was originally chaotic, and Zhu Yuanzhang was a serious person and was extremely dissatisfied with the current version.

He had read the original "History of the Yuan Dynasty" and found it to be shoddy and full of inconsistencies.
